title: STATUS OF EMRSs IN WEST BENGAL
body_text:
The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the  Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the scheme of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for providing quality education to tribal students in their own environment preserving local art and culture. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country. In West Bengal 9 EMRSs have been approved and all are functional. None of the blocks in Alipurduar districts fulfil the prescribed criteria for establishing EMRS.
National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) , an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, provides overall policy direction, academic support, monitoring, capacity building, recruitment, standardization of processes and implementation of the EMRS Scheme across the country. State EMRS Societies oversee the implementation, administration and day-to-day management of EMRSs within their jurisdictions. District Level EMRS Committees , under the Chairmanship of the District Collector/District Magistrate s do local oversight and resolve local implementation issues.
The status of sanctioned, operational and under construction EMRSs in West Bengal, district wise is given at Annexure.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha that 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) have been approved nationally, of which 508 are functional. In West Bengal, all 9 approved EMRSs are functional, with a total enrolment of 3,152 students in 2025-26. Alipurduar district does not meet the criteria for an EMRS as none of its blocks have the required tribal population threshold.
enrichment.context:
EMRS is a flagship scheme under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs aimed at providing quality education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in blocks with significant tribal populations, modeled on Navodaya Vidyalayas but with an emphasis on preserving local art and culture. The scheme criteria requires blocks with over 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons as per Census 2011, which explains why certain districts like Alipurduar are excluded despite having tribal populations. The governance structure involves NESTS (National Education Society for Tribal Students) at the national level for policy and academic oversight, State EMRS Societies for administration, and District Level EMRS Committees chaired by District Collectors for local implementation—reflecting a multi-tier federal implementation model common to many centrally sponsored schemes.

This scheme is significant for UPSC aspirants as it intersects with tribal welfare policy, the Right to Education for marginalized communities, and the broader debate on residential schooling models versus mainstreaming tribal children into regular schools. The scheme has faced scrutiny in Parliament over pace of construction and functional status of approved schools, making such status updates a recurring feature of Parliamentary questions and useful for tracking implementation gaps between sanction and operational functionality.

prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011.

options: National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS)
prelims_questions.explanation: NESTS, an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, is responsible for overall policy direction, academic support, monitoring, and standardization for EMRS implementation nationally.
